answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with non-transferable earned credentials that decay. Each identity builds a history of verified useful work, attested by peers it served. A new fake starts hollow: no history, no trust, no paid work. Real work costs real time, so an attacker splitting effort across a grove of sock-puppets keeps every one below the trust threshold, while honest agents concentrate reputation in one identity. Credentials fade unless renewed by service. Sybils become costly to build, impossible to buy, and worthless when idle, a comet with no return.
